system.name: AGS
system.one_liner: an algorithm-hardware co-designed accelerator for 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM that exploits inter-frame similarity via CODEC-assisted covisibility detection

content.subject: how AGS designates key vs non-key frames and skips low-contribution Gaussians in mapping using recorded pixel counts

elements.name: Frame
elements.role: raw camera frame captured at one timestep by the SLAM system

elements.name: Key Frame / Non-key Frame
elements.role: the frame-type decision resulting from comparing covisibility with ThreshM

elements.name: Full Mapping / Selective Mapping
elements.role: names which mapping procedure runs: baseline 3DGS training on all Gaussians, or skipping the ones already known to be non-contributory

elements.name: Gaussian scene
elements.role: the dashed-border box showing the frame's 3D Gaussians as coloured, numbered ellipses

elements.name: GS_n (Gaussian ellipse)
elements.role: one numbered 3D Gaussian splat; solid colour when computed, grey with a dashed outline when skipped by prediction

elements.name: Gaussian Contribution Information
elements.role: a table recording, per Gaussian ID, how many pixels it contributed negligibly to

elements.name: Thresh_M
elements.role: the covisibility threshold that separates key from non-key frames

elements.name: Thresh_alpha
elements.role: the alpha threshold below which a Gaussian is non-contributory to a given pixel

elements.name: Thresh_N
elements.role: the non-contributory pixel-count threshold (=2 in this example) above which a Gaussian is skipped in later non-key frames

relations.what: a frame's covisibility with the previous key frame decides its designation
key frames run Full Mapping; non-key frames run Selective Mapping
the chosen mapping procedure produces or reuses this frame's Gaussian scene
thresholding each Gaussian's alpha per pixel populates its non-contributory pixel count
a key frame's recorded counts, compared against Thresh_N, mark which Gaussian IDs to grey out and skip in the next non-key frame's scene
covisibility above ThreshM keeps the next frame non-key; covisibility below ThreshM starts a new key frame

panels.label: Frame_t (key frame)
panels.differs: baseline: runs Full Mapping on all four Gaussians (1,2,3,4) and records each one's non-contributory pixel count in a fresh table

panels.label: Frame_t+1 (non-key frame)
panels.differs: high covisibility (> ThreshM) with Frame_t triggers Selective Mapping, which greys out and skips GS2 and GS3 using Frame_t's recorded counts (both >= ThreshN=2) instead of recomputing them

panels.label: Frame_t+2 (key frame)
panels.differs: low covisibility (< ThreshM) with the prior key frame ends the skip streak: a new key frame runs Full Mapping again on a changed Gaussian set (2,3,4,5) and records a fresh contribution table

values.what: the per-Gaussian non-contributory pixel counts in each table (0,3,3,1 for Frame_t; 2,1,3,0 for Frame_t+2) and the ThreshN=2 comparison
values.linked_by: colour (grey row = at/above ThreshN, flagged) and matching GS_n numbers between the ellipse scene and the table rows
values.result_cells: grey-highlighted table rows name exactly which Gaussians (GS2, GS3 in this example) get skipped in the following non-key frame

content.key_idea: A key frame runs full 3DGS mapping and records each Gaussian's non-contributory pixel count; as long as covisibility stays high, later non-key frames reuse that record to skip the same low-contribution Gaussians, until falling covisibility forces a fresh key frame.
content.reading_order: left to right across three time-ordered frames: camera frame, then down through the mapping-type arrow into the Gaussian-splat scene, then down into the contribution table; a key frame's table feeds the skip decision drawn into the next non-key frame's scene

palette.used_for: pale yellow fill of table rows/cells for Gaussians still counted as contributory
blue text marking the Gaussian IDs flagged as non-contributory in each table, and the 'Skip GS2, GS3' annotation
grey fill of flagged table rows and of the skipped Gaussian ellipses in the non-key frame's scene
very light grey background fill of each dashed-border Gaussian-scene box
light purple fill of Gaussian ellipse 4
pale blue fill of Gaussian ellipse 2 when not flagged

style.stroke: thin black outlines; dashed black border around each Gaussian-scene box; dashed blue outlines ring the skipped ellipses in the non-key frame
style.arrows: thick black arrows for the mapping/evaluation pipeline; thin grey elbow arrows for the covisibility-comparison loop above the frames
style.font: sans-serif (Calibri), small (3.5-6.5pt) table text with larger bold headings
style.icons: photographic camera-frame thumbnails; Frame_t and Frame_t+1 reuse the identical photo (illustrating high covisibility) while Frame_t+2 shows a visibly shifted viewpoint

encoding.color_means: yellow = a Gaussian or table row still contributing, grey = a Gaussian or table row marked non-contributory (skip candidate), blue text = the specific Gaussian IDs flagged for skipping, red/purple/pale-blue = individual Gaussian identities 3/4/2 tracked across frames
encoding.line_style_means: dashed borders mark the Gaussian-scene boxes and, in the non-key frame, ring the specific ellipses being skipped; solid arrows carry the mapping/evaluation control flow
encoding.state_means: key vs non-key frame is told apart by the mapping-type label (Full vs Selective) and by whether the scene's Gaussians are solid-coloured (computed) or grey/dashed (skipped via prediction)
encoding.marker_means: numbers on each ellipse are Gaussian IDs (GS_n) kept consistent across frames so the reader can track the same Gaussian being kept or skipped
encoding.emphasis: the same grey fill and dashed blue outline applied to GS2/GS3 in both the table and the scene link the two representations and highlight exactly what selective mapping skips
reusable_patterns: three time-ordered columns sharing one template (photo -> mapping arrow -> annotated scene -> data table)
a small worked data table whose flagged rows are cross-referenced by colour into the diagram above it
a feedback arrow carrying one frame's recorded values into the next frame's decision
weaknesses: the top covisibility-comparison arrows and the bottom mapping pipeline are drawn separately without an explicit connecting line, so the reader must infer that one produces the label the other consumes
Gaussian numbering is not exhaustive (Frame_t+2 jumps from 2 to 5), which could confuse readers about whether Gaussian 1 disappeared or was simply not drawn

summary: This figure walks through AGS's Gaussian contribution-aware mapping across three time-ordered frames. Frame_t is a key frame: it runs Full Mapping over its four Gaussians, then records each one's non-contributory pixel count (from thresholding alpha per pixel) in a Gaussian Contribution Information table; GS2 and GS3 both score 3, at or above ThreshN=2, so they are flagged with grey rows and blue IDs. Because Frame_t+1 has covisibility above ThreshM with Frame_t, it is designated non-key and reuses that table to run Selective Mapping, skipping GS2 and GS3 (drawn grey with dashed outlines) instead of recomputing them. Frame_t+2's covisibility instead falls below ThreshM, so it becomes a fresh key frame, runs Full Mapping on its own changed Gaussian set, and records a new contribution table, restarting the cycle.
summary_zh: 该图按时间演化展示AGS的高斯贡献感知建图：关键帧frame_t全量建图并记录各高斯非贡献像素数，GS2、GS3达阈值被标记；高共视的frame_t+1据此跳过它们做选择性建图；共视度低的frame_t+2则成为新关键帧重新全量建图。
